newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate 10.2 vs 9.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate 10.2 vs 9.2 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate jumped to 10.2 percent on Monday from 9.4 percent, boosted by a stronger volume of fresh term loans.
Dealers said trade totalled 44.2 million kuna, against supply of 69 million.
They put new borrowings at 28.2 percent, mostly granted at a steady 9.0-percent call money rate. Other interbank loans were made between 11 and 15 percent, depending on terms.
Insurers rolled over previous loans at 9.0 percent, teh charge for one-week funds, and 15 percent for one-month kuna.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates weaker at 5.5635 against the dollar and at 3.5607 versus the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4550893
